top_story.headline: Navy award of more than $1 billion to RTX Corporation for aircraft propulsion spares becomes public, three months after signing
top_story.dek: The $1.08 billion order for "propulsion initial spares" is the largest contract action in today's data.
paragraphs: The Department of the Navy obligated $1,081,885,601 to RTX Corporation on a new award whose entire description reads "PROPULSION INITIAL SPARES." It was signed July 30 and only now published on USAspending; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay, so this is not a new signing.

The product category is gas turbines and jet engines for aircraft and their components, and the industry code is aircraft engine and engine parts manufacturing. The record does not say which aircraft or engine program the spares support, or whether the award was competed, so those questions are open.
The amount is the sum obligated so far on the award, and no other contract action in today's USAspending pull comes close to it.

sections.headline: Coast Guard plans sole-source deal with Defense Maritime Solutions for engine inspection work on cutter Healy
paragraphs: 151 new combined synopsis/solicitations, almost all Defense Logistics Agency parts requests; one was moved to the Washington, D.C. section. The one item worth a card comes from a document read today on a notice posted earlier.

blocks.title: Coast Guard plans no-bid contract with Defense Maritime Solutions for engine salvage inspection on cutter Healy
blocks.text: A Notice of Intent attached to this notice, posted October 21 and read today, says the U.S. Coast Guard intends to award a sole-source contract to Defense Maritime Solutions of Chesapeake, Virginia. The work is troubleshooting and technical support on the cutter Healy for "Main propulsion diesel engine component salvage inspection." The notice says the intended contractor is Defense Maritime Solutions and gives no value.

Routine: Defense Logistics Agency Land and Maritime, 82; Defense Logistics Agency Aviation, 52; Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, 16. Most point to the agency's DIBBS portal for the solicitation itself.

sections.headline: Air Force surveys airlines for overseas military working dog shipping
paragraphs: Both new sources-sought notices were flagged; the attachments for both are queued to be read in a later edition.

blocks.title: Air Force asks airlines how they could fly military working dogs overseas
blocks.text: The Department of the Air Force's 773rd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron wants to learn which companies and size classes could provide overseas shipping of military working dogs. The notice uses industry code 481112, scheduled freight air transportation, and says a solicitation will be published in SAM.gov after responses are reviewed. No value or response deadline appears in the text read so far.

items: Veterans Affairs asks companies about armored car services for its Network Contract Office 17. The description points to an attachment that has not yet been read. (36C257-27-AP-0929)

sections.headline: Energy Department adds about $1.33 billion in funding to five lab and site contracts; Veterans Affairs hospital construction award tops new deals
paragraphs: 19 new awards of $2 million or more (1 from the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases, the RTX Corporation award in today's Top Story), 10 large modifications and 2 cuts. 23 routine actions are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Richard Group LLC received a $64,910,819 new award from the Department of Veterans Affairs, signed October 30. The description reads "EHRM PITTSBURG UD," and the product category is construction of hospitals and infirmaries. The record does not spell out the project scope.

Perimeter Solutions LP had $67 million removed from a Forest Service fire retardant contract, described as "FAM RETARDANT - FULL SERVICE, 2026 IQ-NOCOMMIT," on October 15. It is a funding-only action, so it likely returns unused money; the description does not say the work was ended or reduced.

sections.headline: Office of Management and Budget places oversight hold on over $1.2 million for Department of Labor training grants
paragraphs: The Office of Management and Budget flagged one apportionment file carrying an oversight hold during the recent tracking window. The action restricts funding obligations for a Department of Labor training account until specific administrative documentation is supplied.
Routine apportionments for various other bureaus and accounts also moved forward across multiple federal agencies without flags.

footer.coverage_window: October 31-November 1, 2026 (Pacific time), with a trailing sweep for USAspending contract actions plus the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. Of the 14 attachments on 5 notices this edition, 13 were unread and queued for a later edition, and 8,040 files in all are queued for later editions; the Kuwait justification was judged from its notice text only, with no document read. About 160 links to outside portals (mostly the Defense Logistics Agency's DIBBS) were not followed. The Office of Management and Budget section carries no stated gaps.
